To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose efficient routing schemes for k-chordal and chordal graphs, respectively, that are based on a novel distributed algorithm that uses only O(logn)-bits messages and takes O(min{@D, D}) time.
we propose a distributed routing scheme for chordal graphs which uses addresses of size log n bits and local memory size of 2(log n - 1) bits and achieves additive stretch of 2.

(i) for k-chordal networks with diameter D and maximum degree d, we propose a distributed routing algorithm with O(logn)-size messages, O(D) time and local memory of 2(d-2)logn bits, and (ii) for chordal networks with diameter @D and maximum degree d we propose a distributed computation of routing with O(logn) messages, O(min{@DD, n}) time, and local memory of O(logn) bits.

efficient routing algorithms in generalized chordal graph classes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed routing schemes are the most efficient ones known so far for the classes of chordal and k-chordal networks.

our routing schemes provide the following properties: 1) additive stretch of k-2 in k-chordal networks, 2) additive stretch of 0 in chordal networks, 3) routing table size O(logn) bits per node, 4) local memory of size O(logn d) bits per node (d is the maximum degree), and 5) routing table computation time O(min{@D,n}) time, with O(logn)-bits messages.
the proposed routing scheme for chordal graphs is the first one that achieves the additive stretch of 0, and it has the same time and space complexities as the best routing scheme for general graphs.

, in the context of routing, the class of k- chordal graphs can be considered as a natural extension of the class of chordal graphs.
